lines.text: Obamacare prices are jumping again. Sign-ups start tomorrow.
lines.say: Obamacare prices are jumping again. Sign-ups start tomorrow.

lines.text: Open enrollment for 2027 plans begins November 1 in most states.
lines.say: Open enrollment for twenty twenty-seven plans begins November first in most states.

lines.text: KFF says the benchmark silver plan is up 13% on average.
lines.say: KFF says the benchmark silver plan is up thirteen percent on average.

lines.text: That's 11% in HealthCare.gov states, 16% where states run their own.
lines.say: That's eleven percent in HealthCare dot gov states, sixteen where states run their own.

lines.text: A 40-year-old's average benchmark was $625 a month this year. Plus 13%? Our math: about $706.
lines.say: A forty-year-old's average benchmark was six hundred twenty-five dollars a month this year. Plus thirteen percent? Our math: about seven hundred six.

lines.text: Subsidies follow that benchmark, so aid usually rises too. No subsidy? You pay it all.
lines.say: Subsidies follow that benchmark, so aid usually rises too. No subsidy? You pay it all.

lines.text: Earn over 400% of the poverty line? Then there's no federal subsidy.
lines.say: Earn over four hundred percent of the poverty line? Then there's no federal subsidy.

lines.text: Federal data show about 3 million fewer people had marketplace coverage this February than last.
lines.say: Federal data show about three million fewer people had marketplace coverage this February than last.

lines.text: On HealthCare.gov, the deadline for January 1 coverage is December 15. Some state sites run later.
lines.say: On HealthCare dot gov, the deadline for January first coverage is December fifteenth. Some state sites run later.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Obamacare benchmark plans rise 13% for 2027. Who pays?
post.ig:
Obamacare prices are jumping again, and sign-ups start Nov 1.
KFF: 2027 benchmark silver premiums rise 13% on average (11% in HealthCare.gov states, 16% in state-run ones).
A 40-year-old's average benchmark was $625/month in 2026; +13% is about $706 (our math).
Subsidies rise with the benchmark; no subsidy means paying the full increase. On HealthCare.gov, the deadline for Jan 1 coverage is Dec 15; some state sites run later.
Sources: KFF, CMS, HealthCare.gov.
News and education, not financial advice.
